GOV.reason: The complaint is not a finding and does not alone set GOV or G1. Independently, connected capital allocation, unclear current rights deployment and inconsistent material private-loan repayment terms leave minority-protection evidence incomplete.

MOAT.reason: Distribution registrations, client relationships and an operating consulting subsidiary establish a business. Falling commission income, fee outsourcing history and absence of verified retention/take-rate or proprietary barriers limit demonstrated pricing power.

REV.reason: Three-year reported operations CAGR is 27.0%, but FY2023 professional/consultancy expense 2.3962 crore and FY2026 salaried delivery expense 4.5167 crore show a material gross-versus-retained economic mix change. FY2022 outsourcing 12.93 crore against 12.26 crore cost further invalidates the five-year headline. A like-for-like retained-revenue bridge is unavailable; no unsupported organic-growth requirement is imposed.

DUR.reason: Financial distribution/consulting and organically established subsidiary offer runway; new associate capital supports another channel. Commission contraction, material new funding requirement and unproven lending vintages limit durable funded-runway evidence.

CAP.reason: Financial-holding adaptation requires sustainable risk-adjusted ROE and subsidiary capital needs. Historical group ROE about 19.87% is reported arithmetic, not incremental lending return; new 15.28 crore capital commitment and absent loan-vintage/provision/ALM details prevent score.

CASH.reason: Core fee receipts plausibly positive after financing/investment reclassification; historical fee CFO positive in FY2023/24. Concentrated private credit, no verified borrower realization and financing within operating cash prevent strong realization credit. Not mechanically penalized using industrial CFO/PAT.

BAL.reason: March debt/equity 14.75% looks modest, but cash 0.0731 crore is tiny relative to 15.2775 crore subsequent subscription and private assets may not be readily liquid. Current financing/rights completion and demand-loan terms are material unresolved resilience inputs.

EXEC.reason: Subsidiary revenue and consolidated earnings grew, with actual investment/property activity. Parent operating revenue and profit declined, fee mix has been volatile and rights completion is unverified; repeatable allocation success is not demonstrated.

EARN.reason: Group PAT growth 21.18% is real reported growth and core EBIT rises 19.87%. Roughly half pre-associate profit comes from other income, while fee cost mix and cash presentation obscure recurrence; no automatic fraud or restatement deduction.

L.reason: September 24 last observed quote is stale and sparse observed dates cannot support daily execution; a lot consumes one-third of position. Observed turnover proxies do not resolve missing sessions, spread, circuit or BSE restrictions, so liquidity credit is low rather than presumed untradeable.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Conditional hold: a fee business plus concentrated private credit, property and associate investments. Full five-year operating/SOTP and funding models are complete, but current rights funding and asset realization remain material uncertainties. Cash totals reconcile; the separately disclosed legal complaint is an allegation, not a finding. Group FY2026 PAT was ₹4.6683 crore, but parent PAT declined. The ₹15.2775 crore approved associate subscription is 59.16% of March equity. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, not zero. [S1][S5][S6][S7]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Dharni Capital Services Limited, BSE SME 543753, ISIN INE0M9Q01011, listed January 31, 2023; formerly Dharni Online Services. The group includes 100%-owned Dharni Consulting and a 49.28% equity-accounted interest in Dhanayu Finance, incorporated August 31, 2024. Cutoff October 20, 2026; five-year horizon, 15% nominal pretax hurdle and ₹5 lakh illustrative position. March balances are historical, not current holdings. All four gates are Conditional. Official lot 3000 and shares 20.37 million are cross-checked; September 24 secondary ₹55.25 is stale, not an October 19 close. Weakest material confidence is low for current funding, recovery and executable valuation. [S1][S4][S5][S8][S9]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical partial factors are MOAT 4, DUR 5, CASH 4, EXEC 4, EARN 4 and L 2. GOV, REV, CAP, BAL, R, D and P are NS for the specific evidence gaps in the factor audit. BQS coverage is 48%, bounded 2.54–7.22; GQS coverage 45%, bounded 2.55–7.50; IAS coverage 10%, bounded 1.10–9.20. Missing factors are not reweighted. There is no demonstrated G1 failure, critical G2 reliability hold, G3 failure or proven untradeability. The complaint does not mechanically determine governance; unmodified audit likewise is not reassurance on private-credit recovery. [S1][S2][S5][S6][S7][S9]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Revenue combines financial-product commissions and professional/technical consulting. FY2026 commission income ₹2.1097 crore fell 12.04%, while professional services ₹7.4435 crore rose 80.45%; staff expense increased from ₹1.3020 crore to ₹4.5167 crore. Dharni Consulting contributed ₹3.9977 crore revenue and ₹1.5233 crore PAT. Separate investment income and associate profit are not customer revenue. The 2023 IPO raised ₹10.74 crore gross, with ₹8 crore subsidiary investment and ₹2.4085 crore net general-purpose objects. Subsidiary capital of ₹8.01 crore is consistent with deployment but not a complete utilization certificate. [S1][S3][S4]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Registrations, distribution relationships and a functioning consultancy establish a real business, but not a proprietary moat. Retention, take rates, client concentration and switching costs are not sufficiently verified. Professional delivery now has a much larger salaried cost base, while commissions declined; the old outsourcing spread and the current staffing economics should not be treated as identical. Competition and customer renewal matter more than broad financial-market growth. MOAT 4 reflects limited demonstrated pricing power rather than an absent business. [S1][S2][S3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY2021/22 parent operations were ₹2.5541/14.6528 crore and PAT ₹0.1527/0.9658 crore. FY2023–26 group operations were ₹4.7014, ₹8.1981, ₹6.5236 and ₹9.5532 crore; PAT ₹1.1906, ₹3.1071, ₹3.8523 and ₹4.6683 crore. Five-year reported revenue CAGR is about 30.2% and three-year 27.0%, but FY2022 outsourcing of ₹12.93 crore carried ₹12.26 crore professional costs. FY2023 also had ₹2.3962 crore professional expense, whereas FY2026 delivery is staff-heavy. Without a retained-value bridge, these are not comparable organic economic growth scores. Current group revenue growth of 46.44% contrasts with parent decline of 7.58%. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Distribution and consulting offer opportunity, but funded growth must be judged with fee retention and staff productivity. Group PAT divided by average FY2025/26 equity is about 19.87%, not a pure service ROIC or a proven incremental lending return. March associate book value ₹6.4670 crore is equity accounting, not independent fair value. April approval contemplated ₹15.2775 crore of cash rights subscription, intended to preserve 49.28%; current allotment, payment and funding remain unverified. The annual models explicitly separate associate retained profits and cash dividends and test debt or equity funding. CAP remains NS without credit vintages, provisioning, ALM and sustainable new-capital returns. [S1][S5]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Director salaries totaled about ₹0.72 crore, 15.4% of group PAT; the MD loan closed at ₹2.35 crore. Related associate funding and inconsistent CARO wording on repayment terms of the ₹7 crore private loan warrant the underlying contracts, not an inference of wrongdoing. September 18 voting approved all three resolutions, including BSD & Co. for a second five-year auditor term; 170 shareholders were on the record date and 11 members attended. This is a procedural fact, not recovery assurance. In its 3 August 2026 filing, Dharni Capital Services said that it and managing director Hemant Dharnidharka received an ED/PMLA complaint on 2 August alleging assistance with layering and laundering transactions involving Rs 12.54 crore. The filing describes a charge-sheet under Sections 44 and 45 while also saying no formal charges or orders had been passed. The company said there was no immediate material financial or operational impact, it continued operating normally, and it was exploring legal remedies and defending its position. A 4 August supplement specified the alleged transaction period as 1 May 2021 to 30 April 2022. These are allegations disclosed by the company, not a finding of guilt; no subsequent adjudication has been verified in this review. Current encumbrance and subsequent court status remain unverified. [S1][S5][S6][S7][S12][S13]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY2023–26 reported CFO was ₹1.1121, ₹3.5048, ₹0.2965 and −₹1.2202 crore; capex ₹0.6807, ₹6.3625, ₹5.4624 and ₹1.1216 crore. FY2026 closing cash reconciles. Reported CFO includes ₹3.4308 crore borrowing and a ₹7 crore investment-loan outflow and starts with noncash associate profit. Reclassification gives a ₹2.0643 crore fee-cash sensitivity, not an audited corrected CFO. The ₹0.4665 crore dividend/interest label conflict does not change the total ₹2.9738 crore income deduction. Core EBIT is ₹2.9369 crore versus about ₹2.45 crore prior year; roughly half pre-associate profit is other income, whose counterparties and asset realizations cannot be assumed recurring. PPE reconciles as 12.2659 + 1.1216 − 2.3943 − 0.2719 = 10.7213. Model opening WC is actual −₹0.2986 crore after separating flats and property deposits. Full opening assets less liabilities reconcile to ₹25.8257 crore equity. These findings warrant conditional reliability, not unexplained missing-cash allegations. [S1][S2][S4]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At stale ₹55.25 and 20.37 million shares, reference capitalization is ₹112.5443 crore, trailing P/E 24.11 and P/B 4.36. The linked FY2027–31 SOTP separately forecasts service earnings, actual WC, capex, cash tax, half-year borrowing interest, private-credit collections, associate rights/retentions and debt. Bear/base/bull fee growth is −5%/10%/20%, service EBITDA margin 18%/28%/34% and terminal service EV/EBITDA 5×/8×/10×. Rights cash is charged once, with full debt/equity alternatives and matching share dilution. Operating PPE is not added again to service EV; recovered loan principal is removed from terminal assets. Terminal per-share values are ₹0.00/₹33.04/₹69.43, corresponding to annual returns -100.0%/-9.8%/4.7%. These are conditional sensitivities, not targets. Current rights funding, private-credit recovery, associate credit quality and executable price are material low-confidence inputs, so R/D/P and IAS remain NS. [S1][S5][S9]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The permanent-loss path is weaker retained fees combined with illiquid private assets, interest-heavy associate funding and dilution. The full severe model contracts fees 15% annually, uses 10% service EBITDA margin, writes down half the opening private loan without a second cash payment, assumes no principal recovery, a negative 5% associate ROE, 16% borrowing and lower terminal recoveries. Credit impairment lowers earnings and the asset and is added back in cash; it is not an extra cash outflow or replacement WC. Even if assets ultimately recover, a 3000-share lot costs ₹165,750 at the stale quote, one-third of the illustrative position. Fifteen observed dates and low×volume median ₹195,150 are not executable turnover or proof absent sessions were zero. Counterevidence is positive core profit growth, reconciled cash and possible asset recovery. No damages equal to the alleged transaction amount are assumed. [S1][S5][S6][S8][S9]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× requires 37.97% annual per-share appreciation and ₹276.25 terminal value; 10× requires 58.49% and ₹552.50. The bull SOTP reaches ₹69.43, or 1.26× the stale reference price, without claiming extraordinary lending returns or private-asset revaluations. Debt/equity funding sensitivities expose the per-share cost of growth. No evidence currently supports a 5×/10× classification. Higher reported PAT or a bigger associate book alone is not a multibagger thesis. [S1][S5][S9]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: First obtain rights payment, allotment, current ownership and funding, then reconcile cash and debt since March. Verify Aparoksha loan terms, contractual due dates and actual receipts; private balances are not liquid cash. Compare commission receipts with ₹2.1097 crore and staff cost productivity with ₹4.5167 crore. Require lending asset-quality, provisioning, capital adequacy and ALM data before CAP scoring. Obtain a corrected analytical cash classification bridge, current encumbrances and updated company/court status without inferring guilt from a complaint. Refresh the actual BSE quote, lot, depth and restrictions. September voting and October 7 routine demat certification do not resolve these financial questions. [S1][S5][S6][S7][S8][S9][S11][S12]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed conditional deep review, not a quality-compounder or investment-ranking candidate. Historical primary reports, prospectus, group scope, financing, cash classifications, material legal disclosure, post-annual voting and full annual operating/SOTP scenarios have been reviewed. All gates are Conditional with specific limits; no critical failure is inferred solely from drafting, a complaint or uncalibrated scenario probabilities. Aggregate scores remain NS because current funding, private-asset realization and comparable retained growth are material unresolved inputs. The legal disclosure remains an allegation, not an adjudicated finding.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual reports, prospectus and signed issuer filings support historical facts; Business Standard mirrors preserve the observed BSE attachment UUIDs. September 18 voting/auditor and October 7 demat filings were read. Investor directory and cutoff public searches did not establish rights completion or later adjudication; absence of a located update is not proof none exists. Secondary historical OHLCV is not official exchange turnover. All future margins, yields, ROE, recoveries, multiples and funding branches are labeled analyst assumptions. The models retain actual opening balances and reconcile annual cash and balance sheets; they do not solve the current-funding information gap by assertion. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S9][S10][S11][S12][S13]

gates.reason: Connected capital allocation and inconsistent private-loan repayment wording need clarification. The disclosed complaint and company response are not an adjudication or a verified integrity failure.

Audited closing cash and PPE reconcile. Material financing/investment items in reported CFO require an explicit analytical reclassification, now provided; this is not unexplained missing cash or by itself a critical reliability hold. Recurrence of investment income and credit realization remain uncertain.

The 15.2775 crore rights subscription is large relative to 0.0731 crore March cash. Full annual models quantify borrowing and equity alternatives, but actual payment, lender capacity, rollover terms and recoveries are unverified. Modeled financing is conditional, not evidence of an actual funding failure.

Stale September 24 secondary quote, 15 observed dates and a 3000-share lot materially constrain execution. Missing dates are not zero-filled; neither suspension nor BSE surveillance clearance is established.

limitations: No exchange turnover, live depth, BSE surveillance clearance or current executable quote.

methodology: All scenario assumptions are analyst sensitivities, not management guidance or probabilities. Actual March 31 balances are rolled forward from FY2027; they are not claimed to be current October balances.

April approved rights cash is charged once in FY2027 and added once to the owned associate investment book. The issuer intended to preserve 49.28%; actual completion, funding and current ownership are not verified. No associate gross revenue is consolidated or invented. Owned book value earns an assumed after-tax ROE; dividends reduce that book and enter cash once.

Fee EBITDA excludes all historical other income and equity-accounted associate earnings. Only explicit private-credit and securities cash yields are added. Historical property/structured investment income of 2.9738 is not extrapolated as a recurring coupon. Service EV plus nonoperating assets avoids capitalizing investment income twice.

PPE is retained in the operating asset roll-forward and is not added separately to service enterprise value. No independently verified excess-property market value is assumed. Plots 4.0000 and flat advances 1.1294 are separate nonoperating assets, valued only at stated terminal recovery factors. Their 0.3200 security deposit liability is deducted. Other nonoperating assets 0.1175 are excluded from terminal recovery.

Private-credit principal recoveries reduce the asset; recovered principal is not taxed as income or also retained in terminal NAV. Severe impairment is noncash, reduces the loan asset and earnings, and is added back in the cash bridge. It is not a second cash payment or replacement working capital.

Actual negative opening fee WC is used, with forecast ratios applied only to future balances. Half-year average opening/closing debt interest and cash tax are solved simultaneously. New borrowing is conditional availability, not a committed facility. All annual balance sheets and cash bridges reconcile.

Cash floor 0.10, 25% tax on positive fee/financial taxable earnings, no speculative impairment tax shield, and no shareholder dividends. Equity-funding alternatives raise matching cash and new shares at stale reference price or 25% discount. These are dilution sensitivities, not approved issue terms.
Legal complaint amount is not a fine, damages estimate or modeled cash loss. No hypothetical legal settlement is capitalized. The operating/credit severe case is independent of allegations.
valuation.return_formula: Terminal value per diluted share / stale reference price, raised to 1/5, minus 1; no shareholder dividends.
valuation.funding_capacity_warning: Debt is a residual required-funding calculation, not a bank sanction. The bear and severe paths reach unsustainable leverage and floored terminal equity; they are not presented as feasible going-concern borrowing plans. Actual lender capacity, asset saleability and equity access must be established. No approved financing is inferred from the model.
valuation.historical_income_recurrence_warning: The assumed private-credit coupon is a sensitivity on the verified 7 crore balance, not a verified contractual yield. Historical other income includes several developer/financial counterparties not simply the closing asset portfolio. Unidentified recurring income is excluded rather than assigned to invented assets.

limitations: Current rights payment/funding/ownership not verified despite review of annual, issuer directory and April primary filing.
Court disposition and updated company response not verified; complaint is not a finding.
Historical gross outsourcing versus retained-value growth prevents comparable REV score; not an organic-scope assumption alone.
Borrower realization, loan terms, current encumbrance, credit vintages and asset fair values remain unverified.
No current exchange-verified executable quote or BSE surveillance determination.
next_steps: Resolve material current capital and cash bridge before aggregate scoring or valuation.
Verify subsequent issuer or authority updates to the disclosed legal matter.
